A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Distillation Robustifies Unlearning and retain the same core study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching the original appendices to their relocated counterparts.

before.justification: v1 reports original oracle-matching, unlearning, distillation, and robustness experiments on language, arithmetic, and WMDP tasks.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original TOFU training, relearning, and quantization-attack results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F add a post-training adaptation: distill the unlearned model into its original pretrained checkpoint, assuming that checkpoint never possessed the target knowledge. This changes student initialization for the new setting; the main UNDO corruption rule and distillation procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds TOFU fictional-author question answering, with target knowledge introduced through finetuning. This substantially extends coverage to forgetting newly acquired factual associations. The original English/Korean, arithmetic, and WMDP Bio/Cyber coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding language, arithmetic, and WMDP experiments retain their comparator sets, including GradDiff, MaxEnt, RMU, SAM, RepNoise, and UNDIAL where previously evaluated. TOFU extends the existing unlearning-only versus distillation comparison with a never-exposed model control; no new competing unlearning method is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces substantial new evaluation protocols: TOFU finetuning and distillation with Gemma-2-2B and Phi-1.5, 100-update relearning against clean-base controls, additional QA/extraction/membership-inference/utility metrics, and FP16-versus-INT4 evaluation. The original experiments' settings and hyperparameter tables are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F tests whether pretrained students lacking the target knowledge can reproduce the robustness effect. It also adds a distinct robustness question absent from v1: whether quantization restores forgotten knowledge. Figures 12–13 and Table 14 extend the analyses beyond the original initialization/noise studies and finetuning attacks.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed medians and error bars in Figure 5, four-seed WMDP averages, and preprocessing seed 42. The added TOFU experiments disclose no additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 13 averages metrics rather than reporting seed uncertainty.

E6.justification: Figures 12–13 add TOFU training and relearning findings for two model families. Table 14 newly reports INT4 forget truth ratios of 0.185 for GradDiff and 0.017 after distillation, with utilities of 0.242 and 0.391 respectively. These substantial new results supplement largely retained original findings.

T1.justification: Section 4 corrects the displayed RMU objective by adding the coefficient alpha to the preservation loss. Nonunit alpha settings already appeared in v1's appendix, so this is a limited mathematical specification correction rather than evidence of a changed experiment. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about oracle matching, distillation robustness, and UNDO's compute tradeoff. The headline claims of oracle-like robustness using 60–80% of the compute and 0.01% labeled pretraining data are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F explains the clean-student assumption, qualifications concerning latent knowledge despite dataset novelty, and a proposed interpretation of quantization robustness. Appendix D.2.5 also removes v1's unsupported expectation that TAR would fail across all their settings, retaining the reported training-budget limitation.

D1.justification: v3 identifies OpenUnlearning as the implementation framework for the added TOFU and quantization experiments and specifies full-TOFU distillation inputs and clean pretrained students. Existing hyperparameter tables, corruption pseudocode, hardware/time disclosures, and GitHub access remain unchanged. The new experiments receive comparatively limited implementation detail.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to OpenUnlearning, The Elicitation Game, membership inference attacks, and Unlearning Isn't Deletion, supporting the new implementation, attack discussion, and corruption interpretation. All earlier cited works are retained, and the main related-work positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, terminology and several passages are edited, and an appendix contents page and post-training extension paragraph are added. New Appendix F precedes the author contributions, relabeled G. The main section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 12–13 and Table 14, recolors several plots, and cleans legends, including SERUM-to-UNDO in Figure 11. Figure 3 omits some plotted sweep trajectories whose endpoint results remain in Appendix B.1. The existing figure organization and table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: Appendix F strengthens empirical support through post-training factual unlearning on two model families and a distinct quantization attack, while clarifying the clean-student assumption. Editorial corrections also improve precision. These are useful but bounded gains: the original WMDP utility and compute limitations remain, and the new experiments lack detailed hyperparameter and uncertainty reporting.
